items.title: Albert Burbank Interview, 1962-01-04
items.q: Henry told me about him so I went to him and I got a few lessons from him.

ctx.x: You think you were more as strong as them too, huh? Yeah.

Oh, what about Elah Bar? That's always been one of these special numbers. How long you been playing that? Oh, since I stopped playing. Well, I know you know plenty of those Creole words and all that. Did your family speak French in the home? Yeah. My mother would speak to us in French and we'd answer her in English because we didn't like it. We didn't say any English. That's why if somebody asked me something, I stumbled to answer that because I know what I want to say but I can't get it out. Do you speak any…

Yeah. It wasn't any efficient. Another thing I want to ask you, Alvin, you wrote some different numbers. I know you wanted to do one at Jean Zamy. It was a tune you'd written. How many tunes have you written?
